question: Does the shallow curvature/load compensation remain a universal source transformation for an exact axisymmetric Helfrich graph, and what condition permits one load correction to preserve two shapes at different tensions?
status_scope: Separate conditional analytic task after the inclusion stage stopped. Lead preliminary variational reasoning preceded this registration; this freezes conventions and checks, not blind theorem discovery.

definitions.geometry: axisymmetric single-valued height h(r), r>=0, p=h_prime, J=sqrt(1+p^2), C=(r*p/J)_prime/r = 2H
definitions.coefficients: known uniform kappa>0, known uniform sigma>0; compare two sigma with the SAME c(r), f(r) and kappa
definitions.source_coordinates: c and f prescribed in projected radial coordinate r, not material labels; this is a modeling assumption
definitions.load: f is vertical dead load per projected area, potential -integral f*h dA_projected; signed net vertical force 2*pi*integral r*f dr =0 including prescribed return load
definitions.boundary: regular origin h_prime(0)=0; h and slope decay to flat reservoir; c and source perturbation g smooth compact support with radial regularity; use compact variations or vanishing boundary work
definitions.perturbation: c -> c+g, choose delta f(r) to preserve a specified stationary h; check finite g, not only infinitesimal

required_checks: vary the full square and full area factor, including c^2 J
derive exact load correction or a counterexample
check total vertical force and boundary terms
recover shallow joint-small-source limit delta f=-kappa*radial_Laplacian(g)
derive criterion for one delta f to preserve TWO specified profiles
include flat-profile or degenerate control case so broken universal symmetry is not claimed global identifiability
distinguish actual equilibria from arbitrary test profiles; no numerical equilibrium or stability claim
stop_condition: One independently checked exact source-compensation criterion or precise derivation blocker. No solver, fit, sweep, biological permission, novelty or global uniqueness claim.
